prompt: White to play and win a man — quietly.

steps.note: b5 is no better — the same man on c4 jumps either way.

explanation: A man on c4 attacks nothing, but it stands in front of both squares the black man on c6 could use — b5 and d5 — so whichever it picks, it is jumped. Meanwhile f5 covers g6, the only move the h7 man has. Every legal black move loses a piece, and that is a fork without a single capture on the board.
source: Composed for GameExplorer

prompt: White to play and win a man — quietly.

steps.note: c2 is covered by the same man on d1.

explanation: The man on d1 already covers c2 and e2 — both squares the black man on d3 can move to — so that man is lost as soon as it has to move. e4–f5 handles the other one by taking g6 away from h7. Black is in what checkers players call a squeeze: every move is a losing move, and no capture was needed to arrange it.
source: Composed for GameExplorer
